A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ClassDiffusion and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Reordered and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original personalization experiments, quantitative comparisons, human preferences, sensitivity analyses, and video-generation examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds TIFA scores, a Prospect comparison, quantitative SPL-weight analysis, and three-concept generation examples.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same personalization procedure and cosine-distance semantic preservation loss added to reconstruction loss. Renaming the loss and explaining the existing K/V tuning and text embeddings do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix F and Figure 13 add simultaneous three-concept generation, extending the paired-concept examples in v1. DreamBooth, Textual Inversion, and CustomConcept101 coverage and the personalized-video task are retained.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated Prospect comparator in Appendix G, Table 2. The five single-concept baselines in Table 1 and the Custom Diffusion comparison for multiple concepts remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds TIFA to single-concept evaluation and quantitative CLIP-T/DINO-I evaluation across five SPL weights. Existing training budgets, inference settings, and the 20-concept, 25-prompt, 20-images-per-prompt protocol are retained. Newly specifying the default SPL weight does not establish a changed setting.

E4.justification: Appendix H and Table 3 add quantitative loss-weight sensitivity analysis to the retained qualitative weight/step sweep. Figure 11 replaces the center-word sensitivity examples, while Figure 3 adds average-activation indicators to the existing attention visualizations.

E5.justification: Both versions state that the qualitative SPL sweep uses the same random seed. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty-reporting procedures.

E6.justification: All pre-existing Table 1 scores are retained. v2 adds TIFA results, including 0.843 for ClassDiffusion and 0.835 for SVDiff, Prospect scores in Table 2, and weight-sensitivity scores in Table 3. Three-concept outputs are added, and center-word examples and dog-video frames are replaced. These are additional or revised results, not demonstrated performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the entropy derivation and assumptions; the conditional-entropy argument moves unchanged from Appendix C to B. Equation 4 restores the class condition already present in Equation 2, a notation-consistency correction rather than a substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central semantic-drift explanation and SPL contribution remain. v2 explicitly states that all tuning-based models inherently suffer from overfitting and refocuses the contribution list on image/video personalization. BLIP2-T remains proposed in the introduction but is removed from the abstract and standalone contribution bullet.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly distinguishes SPL's semantic recovery from DreamBooth prior preservation, recommends finer-grained center words, and interprets the quantitative ablation as showing limited weight sensitivity with weight 1 preferred. The human-face and ambiguous-category limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the default SPL weight as 1.0 and identifies the text encoder as clip-vit-large-patch14. Hardware, timing, and other principal implementation settings are retained. The project-page URL supplied in v1's abstract is removed; this does not establish that the resource itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Prospect, Diffusion4D, ControlVideo, 4DGen, DreamLCM, and diffusion-based image matting. It also more explicitly positions SPL against DreamBooth's prior-preservation objective. The overall personalization research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, experimental-analysis explanation, loss description, and conclusion are rewritten or expanded. Subject-driven preliminaries are added, the contribution narrative is reframed, and appendix sections are reordered. These changes extend beyond isolated copy edits.

P2.justification: The motivating, semantic-space, and distribution diagrams are substantially redrawn. The storytelling figure moves earlier, Table 1 gains TIFA and explicit win-rate labels, and two tables and a three-concept figure are added. Center-word displays are revised, and several retained figures are relocated or substantially resized.

improvement.justification: Table 3 strengthens the previously qualitative sensitivity analysis, and Table 2 adds a relevant competitor. The disclosed SPL weight and clearer user-study win-rate labels improve reproducibility and interpretation. These provide a modest net gain despite sparse setup information for the new evaluations and removal of the project link; the principal results and theoretical arguments remain unchanged.
